final_answer:
Let
\[
\Delta(\lambda,\tau)=\lambda^2+1+\frac{\lambda}{2}e^{-\lambda\tau}.
\]
At \(\tau=0\),
\[
\lambda^2+\frac12\lambda+1=0,
\]
whose roots have real part \(-1/4\), so the system is initially stable.

A stability change can occur only when a root crosses the imaginary axis. Put \(\lambda=i\omega\), \(\omega>0\). Then
\[
-\omega^2+1+\frac{i\omega}{2}(\cos \omega\tau-i\sin\omega\tau)=0,
\]
so
\[
1-\omega^2+\frac{\omega}{2}\sin(\omega\tau)=0,\qquad
\cos(\omega\tau)=0.
\]
Thus \(\sin(\omega\tau)=\pm1\).

If \(\sin(\omega\tau)=1\), then
\[
\omega^2-\frac{\omega}{2}-1=0
\]
so
\[
\omega=a=\frac{1+\sqrt{17}}4.
\]
The corresponding crossing times are
\[
\tau=A_n=\frac{(4n+1)\pi}{2a},\qquad n=0,1,2,\dots
\]

If \(\sin(\omega\tau)=-1\), then
\[
\omega^2+\frac{\omega}{2}-1=0
\]
so
\[
\omega=b=\frac{\sqrt{17}-1}{4}.
\]
The corresponding crossing times are
\[
\tau=B_n=\frac{(4n+3)\pi}{2b},\qquad n=0,1,2,\dots
\]

Now determine crossing direction. Implicit differentiation gives
\[
\lambda'(\tau)=-\frac{\Delta_\tau}{\Delta_\lambda}.
\]
At an imaginary crossing \(\lambda=i\omega\), with \(s=\sin(\omega\tau)=\pm1\), one obtains
\[
\operatorname{sgn}\Re \lambda'(\tau)=\operatorname{sgn}(4s\omega-1).
\]
Hence the \(A_n\)-crossings, where \(s=1\), move roots from left to right, while the \(B_n\)-crossings, where \(s=-1\), move roots from right to left.

Since the system is stable at \(\tau=0\), stability is lost at \(A_0\). It is regained at \(B_0\), then lost again at \(A_1\). After that, the rightward crossings occur frequently enough that the leftward crossings never bring the number of unstable roots back to zero.

Thus the stable intervals are
\[
0<\tau<A_0
\]
and
\[
B_0<\tau<A_1.
\]
Using
\[
a=\frac{1+\sqrt{17}}4,\qquad b=\frac{\sqrt{17}-1}{4},
\]
these become
\[
A_0=\frac{\pi(\sqrt{17}-1)}8,
\]
\[
B_0=\frac{3\pi(\sqrt{17}+1)}8,
\]
\[
A_1=\frac{5\pi(\sqrt{17}-1)}8.
\]

Therefore the complete answer is
\[
\boxed{
\tau\in\left(0,\frac{\pi(\sqrt{17}-1)}8\right)
\;\cup\;
\left(\frac{3\pi(\sqrt{17}+1)}8,\frac{5\pi(\sqrt{17}-1)}8\right).
}
\]
